thread.title: Settlement reached in last of four federal lawsuits against Providence officer - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Settlement reached in last of four federal lawsuits against Providence officer - NewsBreak

author: Alexandra Leslie
title: Settlement reached in last of four federal lawsuits against Providence officer - NewsBreak
text:
By Alexandra Leslie ,
8 hours ago
PROVIDENCE, R.I. (WPRI) — The city of Providence has paid out $126,000 in settlements for an officer who faced four federal lawsuits, Target 12 has learned.
On Tuesday, federal court filings showed that a settlement against Officer Matthew Sheridan had been approved a month earlier by the Providence City Council’s Committee on Claims and Pending Suits.
In all, the city settled in three cases, and a jury exonerated the officer in another case last year.
In the most recent case to settle, Christopher Johnson filed a federal civil rights lawsuit in 2019, accusing Sheridan of unlawfully stopping him in 2016 while he was walking home in South Providence after going out with friends.
Johnson, who was a Rhode Island state poet laureate finalist at the time, said Sheridan asked him for his name without reason. And when he refused to provide it, Sheridan grabbed him by the arm and slammed him against the police cruiser so hard it “dented the rear passenger side door,” according to court records.
Six years later, the case settled for $67,500 and concludes the last of four cases filed against Sheridan, according to his attorney Michael Colucci.
Johnson’s attorney did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
A third case against Sheridan went to trial last year, where a jury ruled the officer didn’t violate the civil rights of two Boston men during an arrest in 2016.
Colucci said the other two cases reached settlement agreements that, “reflect a compromise by all parties with an acknowledgment of no findings of fault on either side.”
One of those settlements came after Esmelin Fajardo filed a civil rights lawsuit against Sheridan and the city in 2018, claiming Sheridan beat him up while ushering out partygoers who were still at a nightclub after closing hours in 2015.
The case was heading to trial in March 2023 before it was settled for $16,000 that August.
In 2017, Charm Howie filed a federal civil rights lawsuit against Sheridan. Howie, who attended the Providence police academy with Sheridan, accused the officer of verbally abusing him outside his home, pushing him into his car and choking him.
The Howie case was set to go to trial in November 2023 before it was settled for $42,500.
Sheridan is still employed by Providence Police, according to Colucci. Budget documents show Sheridan has an annual salary of $81,516.
“He is also a combat veteran, recently elevated to the rank of Major (select) in the United States Army – Infantry Division and one of the city’s finest and most reliable police officers,” Colucci said.
Target 12 reached out to the city multiple times for comment, but did not immediately hear back on Wednesday.
